size_mapping.rule: H (tree leaves + spent nullifiers) a multiple of 80; unspent notes N = H/5; positions P = H/10 over 4 markets; tree leaves L = (H + N)/2 = 3N; spent nullifiers F = H - L = L - N (every spent note left one nullifier)
size_mapping.why: Per batch the keccak work is about 4 permutations per tree leaf (each of the two state roots hashes every leaf and its tree node), 1 per spent nullifier (the decode rebuilds the nullifier chain), and about 2.4 per unspent note and 2.8 per position (the notes and positions digests in the two roots); the counted runs match this to 0.1% (355,413 measured against 355,200 at H = 100,000, phase 0). With L = (H + N)/2 and F = (H - N)/2 that is about 2.5 H + 3.9 N + 2.8 P permutations, increasing in H, N and P. The three admission bounds are enforced separately, so a state with all three at their bounds is the costliest one they admit; that is the shape measured, with N = H/5 and P = H/10, the ratio of the provisional gateway bounds
size_mapping.pre_state: 4 fee-bearing markets at 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,000 / 2,500 USD with a recorded price and a non-zero stored funding rate and carry; traders 2k and 2k+1 hold opposite positions of 0.01 to 0.05 base, equal entry (within 1% of the price) and funding entry, 50 to 62 USD collateral, in every market; note amounts 50 to 146 USD; reserves 5,000 insurance, 2,000 treasury, 1,000 clearing pool; external_in balances the conservation identity; tree depth 24; wind-down recipient set

batches.phase0: Deposit, Fill (taker buys 0.02 from a resting maker, growing both positions), Fill (partial reverse of 0.01), Withdraw to L1, AccrueFunding x2; 4 timed ops in 700 ms, oracle transcripts signed by the public test key
batches.phase1: SettleAll over the whole state at the recorded prices, no shortfall: every position closes inside its collateral and the 8,000 USD of reserves are paid to the wind-down recipient as one withdrawal leaf
batches.phase1-haircut: SettleAll with every market's recorded price at twice the entry level and empty reserves: the short side's losses exceed its collateral, the pro-rata haircut reissues every unspent note, and the tree gains N leaves before the post-state root

calibration.method: tree-depth differential: one leaf, no ops, depths 8/36/64; each level adds one 65-byte MerkleNode hash to decode and to each of the two state roots

precompile_model.status: projection; the precompile build is not measured here
precompile_model.method: Effective cycles if every counted keccak-f permutation ran as SP1's KECCAK_PERMUTE syscall: cycles x (gas - permutations x saving) / gas. saving = gas of the 6,437 tiny_keccak::keccakf instructions at the gas-per-cycle of keccak code (from the calibration) minus the syscall's gas from SP1 6.1.0's own cost tables (sp1-core-executor utils::cost_and_height_per_syscall with artifacts/rv64im_costs.json, vm/gas.rs complexity mapping, report.rs normalization 191). Absorb, padding and loop code around the permutation stay in software. A projection only: the precompile build needs a network fetch and is measured when it is built

gpu_time_model.formula: T(H) = fixed_s + cycles(H) / R; a size fits when T(H) <= prover_budget_s / margin for phase0, phase1 and phase1-haircut
gpu_time_model.prover_budget_source: crates/gateway/src/prover_client.rs: PROVER_TIMEOUT_SECS, default 900 s, bounds each /prove call. crates/gateway/src/l1.rs min_anchor_timeout_ms: the boot handshake requires anchorTimeoutMs >= (2 x FINALITY_BUDGET + PROVER_TIMEOUT_SECS + 300 s) x 1000, FINALITY_BUDGET = 1,200 s (crates/gateway/src/clock_wait.rs). The launch anchor_timeout_ms is 3,600,000 (docs/REDEPLOY-CC-RUNBOOK.md, docs/RELEASE_MANIFEST.md), which admits at most 3,600 - 2,400 - 300 = 900 s of proving
gpu_time_model.fixed_source: the recorded Groth16 wrapping stage of the clock-v2 proof: container 2026-10-09T18:27:56.49Z to 18:32:06.25Z, 249.8 s with 4 CPUs and 13 GB (docs/audits/2026-10-09-clock-final/generation.json, .github/workflows/clock-proof-wrap.yml); its input is the constant-size recursion output, so it does not grow with the program
gpu_time_model.rate_assumption: No GPU proving throughput is recorded in this repository. R, the sustained core-plus-recursion proving rate of the launch prover in guest cycles per second, is assumed at 1,000,000 (central) with the sensitivity rows below. The central value is taken at the low end because the hard cap protects a one-shot wind-down proof and is raised only by a measured rate
gpu_time_model.recorded_reference: contracts/integration/fixtures/clock-v2-verified records a real proof of a 6,035,092-cycle clock-v2 execution under SP1 6.1.0; its core and recursion time is not recorded

recommendation.basis: At the central rate the launch budget allows 200,000,000 cycles per proof ((900 s / 2 - 250 s) x 1,000,000 cycles/s). The shortfall variant of phase 1 is the costliest batch at every measured size and sets the cap: at 5,280 history it takes 198,725,972 cycles, at 5,360 it takes 201,728,802. Phase 0 and the solvent phase 1 alone would allow about 6,300 and 6,700. Positions and notes keep the measured ratio, H/10 and H/5. The bound holds for the software and for the precompile build, since the precompile only lowers the cost
recommendation.precompile_decision: Without the precompile the cap is 5,280 at the central rate, below the planned 100,000 (crates/gateway/src/admission.rs). Software keccak reaches 100,000 only at R >= 19.0 M cycles/s sustained, 19x the central assumption; at the gate sizes about 91 to 96% of the cycles are keccak, and the precompile projection lowers the cost per history unit by a factor of about 2.1 (100,000 then needs R >= 8.9 M cycles/s). So the precompile is adopted in this program key
recommendation.after_precompile_build: Re-run this tool on the precompile ELF once it is built with the reviewed recipe and set the caps from its measured cycles with the same formula; the projection at the central rate is about 11,600 history (positions 1,160, notes 2,320)
recommendation.planned_scale: At the launch prover budget, 100,000 history needs a measured R of at least 8.9 M cycles/s with the precompile. The cap scales linearly with R and with the compute seconds per proof, (anchorTimeoutMs / 1000 - 2,700) / 2 - 250; a launch with a larger anchorTimeoutMs gives a proportionally larger cap without a program change

gpu_day: GPU day re-measures: it proves phase 0 and phase 1 (and the shortfall variant) at the configured cap on the launch prover, records the proving time and the sustained rate R, and re-derives the cap with the same formula. This gate fixes the program decision (the precompile) before the program key freezes; the caps are admission policy and change without a new program key
